## Context

See [proposal.md](proposal.md). The ETHOS introduction films stay frozen, and the films of 2.0.1
stay as released. The owner's answer of 28 November 2026 makes one exception for three moves that
change nothing the films are built from: the ETHOS release, Windows out of the ETHOS pin and the
Mise lock, and the GitLab runner label. The rebind follows ETHOS's successor-first adopter cutover:
bind the release in the lane, prove, publish for review, land, and publish the accepted head.

**The GitLab file is generated by ETHOS.** `.config/checks/ci-projection/policy.toml` declares
`.gitlab-ci.yml` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` as `cue` projections that ETHOS compiles from
`.config/ci/pipeline.cue`, the common model `.config/ci/verification.cue` that ETHOS ships, and the
input `.config/ci/verification.toml`. `ethos lane project` writes them, and
`ethos lane project --check` reports a file that differs from its projection as
`generated_projection_drift:<path>`. The runner tags are the input's `[gitlab.runners.macos]`
`review_tags` and `protected_tags`, so they change there and the file follows by projection, never
by hand. Read on 28 November 2026: the film's `.gitlab-ci.yml` differs from filmkit's at `v0.35.0`
only in the two jobs' `tags` lists, its `verification.toml` differs from filmkit's only in those two
lists and the comment above them, and its `runners.toml` and projection policy are the same as
filmkit's. The projection after the change is therefore expected to equal filmkit's `.gitlab-ci.yml`
at `v0.35.0` byte for byte. The common model has no diff between the two ETHOS tags.

**Windows in the Mise supply.** The pin lists `windows-arm64` and `windows-x64`. The lock holds, for
each of its four tools (ETHOS, Node, Python and uv), the platforms `linux-arm64`,
`linux-arm64-musl`, `linux-x64`, `linux-x64-musl`, `macos-arm64` and `windows-x64`; it never held
`windows-arm64`. `.config/mise/config.toml` sets no `lockfile_platforms`, so `mise lock` keeps the
platforms the lock already records (Mise's documentation, as filmkit's archived
`run-ci-on-arm-macos` cites it).

**The published declaration.** `tools/ci/delivery/release_assets.py` at the tag (`assemble`) writes
`ethos-<version>.mise.toml` from the archives that the release legs qualified, one row per platform
in sorted order, and the tag's GitHub workflow calls it with
`--required linux-x64,linux-arm64,macos-arm64 --optional windows-x64,windows-arm64`. ETHOS's own
readback of the release (forge metadata, read on 28 November 2026) lists the asset at 1,299 bytes,
the size that form gives for all five rows, and lists all five archives. The repository's table
takes three of them and reads as below, each checksum read from `SHA256SUMS` and checked against the
asset's published digest:

```toml
# The ETHOS release declaration published with v0.2.0-beta.12: its linux-arm64, linux-x64 and macos-arm64 rows.
[tools."http:ethos"]
version = "0.2.0-beta.12"

[tools."http:ethos".platforms]
linux-arm64 = { url = "https://github.com/HengYangDS/ethos/releases/download/v0.2.0-beta.12/ethos-0.2.0-beta.12-linux-arm64.tar.gz", checksum = "sha256:<SHA256SUMS>", bin_path = "ethos/bin" }
linux-x64 = { url = "https://github.com/HengYangDS/ethos/releases/download/v0.2.0-beta.12/ethos-0.2.0-beta.12-linux-x64.tar.gz", checksum = "sha256:<SHA256SUMS>", bin_path = "ethos/bin" }
macos-arm64 = { url = "https://github.com/HengYangDS/ethos/releases/download/v0.2.0-beta.12/ethos-0.2.0-beta.12-macos-arm64.tar.gz", checksum = "sha256:<SHA256SUMS>", bin_path = "ethos/bin" }
```

ETHOS's own supply pins (Mise floor 2026.11.9, Node 26.13.1, Python 3.14.10, uv 0.13.8, Vale 3.27.0)
are the same at both tags, so the release moves no supply of the repository.

The known open defects under ETHOS's `defects/` at the tag that this lane can meet, each with its
recorded workaround:

- `console-reexecutes-in-selected-runtime`: until the bind, the newer console answers with the
  selected 0.2.0-beta.11 build. Preview with the new runtime's interpreter,
  `<runtime>/python/bin/python -B -I -m ethos.cli`, and read `summary.runtime`.
- `installed-image-bytecode-refuses-hook-install`: one run of that interpreter without `-B` makes
  `hook install` answer `hook_install_failed:hook_runtime_payload_mismatch`. Never run it without
  `-B`; the repair is `mise uninstall` and `mise install` of the release.
- `projection-preview-patch-file-not-written`: the preview of `ethos lane project` names a patch
  file that no command writes. Write the `patch` entry of the preview's JSON result to a file, byte
  for byte, and pass it to `--patch`.
- `command-gate-verdict-follows-launch-shell`: the declared command gates run in the proof's launch
  environment. Launch as decision 5 says.
- `behavior-gate-uv-cache-missing-wheel`: on a host whose uv cache lacks a locked wheel, the
  behavior gate ends with `test_environment_sync_failed`; one online `uv sync --locked` by the
  pinned uv fills the cache.
- `lane-path-day-refusal-names-no-path`: a lane started before 08:00 on 29 November (UTC+8) carries
  the UTC day, 2026-11-28. A refused `--path` names no expected path; it is the `path` field of the
  `--json` result.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**

- Run every gate and lifecycle command of the film, locally and in the hosted jobs, on
  0.2.0-beta.12.
- Leave no Windows row in the ETHOS pin and no Windows table in the Mise lock, and keep every Linux
  one.
- Select the GitLab runners by `macos-latest` with `review` or `protected`, the pipelines staying
  ETHOS's projection of the declaration.
- Keep the 0.2.0-beta.11 runtime as the rollback until the landing is accepted.

**Non-Goals:**

- Changing the films' content, picture or sound, cutting an edition, or tagging a release.
- Changing any source, test, gate or declared command of the film.
- Renaming the gate providers to catalog IDs (decision 4).
- Removing the Windows wheels of `uv.lock` or the template's commented example in
  `openspec/config.yaml`: neither lies in the pin or the Mise lock, and the owner's decision admits
  nothing else.
- Moving other supply, raising the Mise floor or changing the lockfile format; no step runs
  `mise lock --upgrade`.
- Registering, tagging or untagging runners, which belong to ETHOS's governance.

## Decisions

1. **Windows leaves the lock through `lockfile_platforms`.** Options: (a) delete the Windows tables
   by hand; (b) `["linux-arm64", "linux-x64", "macos-arm64"]`; (c) every platform the lock holds
   besides Windows. Chosen: (c), filmkit 0.34.1's form. (a) edits a generated file, and the next
   `mise lock` would keep the platforms it records. (b) would also drop the eight musl tables of the
   four tools, more than Windows, which the reading of 25 November keeps. (c) declares what the lock
   holds, so `mise lock` removes exactly the four `windows-x64` tables. `[settings]` gains
   `lockfile_platforms = ["linux-arm64", "linux-arm64-musl", "linux-x64", "linux-x64-musl", "macos-arm64"]`
   with filmkit's comment line, which names who chose each platform set, by role, and the date. The
   step runs on 0.2.0-beta.11, before the pin moves, so that each of the two lock diffs shows one
   thing.
2. **The pin takes the published rows unchanged.** The three rows that are not Windows go into the
   `[tools."http:ethos"]` table, the form the repository holds, under a comment that names the
   release and the rows it takes, after each checksum is checked against `SHA256SUMS` and the
   published asset digest. The lock keeps `lockfile_version = 3`.
3. **The tags change in the declaration, and the file by projection.** `[gitlab.runners.macos]`
   takes `review_tags = ["macos-latest", "review"]` and
   `protected_tags = ["macos-latest", "protected"]` under filmkit's comment, less its word
   "project-locked", which the record states of filmkit's runners alone: "CI runs only on
   Apple-silicon macOS, and both forges select it by one label: GitHub's hosted `macos-latest`, and
   on GitLab the macOS guest's runners, which carry the same label beside `review` or `protected`
   (the owner's decision of 2026-11-25)." The lane previews with `ethos lane project --json` after
   the bind, writes the preview's `patch` to a file, and applies exactly that with
   `ethos lane project --apply --authorize --expect-head <head> --patch <file>`.
4. **The gate providers keep their legacy names.** The 0.2.0-beta.11 rebind placed their rename in
   this rebind, and 0.2.0-beta.11, now the rollback, resolves the catalog IDs. The owner's decision
   of 28 November admits nothing beyond the three moves, and 0.2.0-beta.12 still resolves the legacy
   names, so the rename is left to a later Change. Each proof notes `gate_provider_legacy_name`,
   which is expected and not a gap.
5. **Every local proof launches as the generated hosted job does:** `mise exec --locked --` around
   the lane runtime's `ethos prove`, in the work tree, never with Mise's activation variables
   removed alone. Under 0.2.0-beta.12 the executed result states it: `summary.environment` names the
   locked tools that the launch path resolves outside their locked install, and the check of each
   declared command gate, all three of which start `uv`, names its `supplier`: `locked` when the
   lock supplies `uv`, and `launch-path` or `unresolved` when the launch environment did, which is a
   finding.
6. **The Changelog states the change since 2.0.1 once.** The films of 2.0.1 ran 0.2.0-beta.10 (the
   tag `v2.0.1` pins it), so the `Unreleased` line that names 0.2.0-beta.11 is edited to name
   0.2.0-beta.12 instead of 0.2.0-beta.10. Under `Changed` one line adds the runner label; under
   `Removed` one line names ETHOS's Windows archives leaving the pin and the four Windows tables
   leaving the Mise lock, the Linux ones kept.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [A gate that passed under 0.2.0-beta.11 fails under 0.2.0-beta.12] → ETHOS's copies run before the
  tag passed a full proof on 12 of 14 governed trees and found no new required gap; it does not name
  the trees, so this tree's result there is not known. If the lane meets a failure, it is repaired
  at its owner, or the repository restores the 0.2.0-beta.11 declaration in a new Change and binds
  the retained runtime.
- [A local verdict depends on the launch environment] → Launch as decision 5 says; the hosted jobs
  of the proposal decide, and they are read before landing.
- [GitLab-hosted CI is not qualified by this beta] → The proposal's GitLab review job, run on the
  new tags on this host's guest under a host ticket, qualifies it for this repository.
- [The proposal is pushed before the runners carry the new tags, and its job waits] → ETHOS's
  governance added them on 28 November and the maintainer read them back; the lane reads them again
  before the push.
- [A pipeline of a commit before this Change, such as the tag `v2.0.1`, selects the old tags] → Once
  ETHOS's governance drops them, such a pipeline finds no runner; they are dropped only after this
  film's `main` is published, and a re-run of an older pipeline then needs them back.
- [A rollback after the bind is not qualified by 0.2.0-beta.12's journey] → A rollback restores the
  0.2.0-beta.11 declaration and lock in a new Change and runs the full proof before it lands.

## Migration Plan

Remove Windows from the pin and the lock, copy the new declaration's rows and lock them, install the
locked supply, bind the runtime, change the runner tags and apply the projection, record the moves,
run the repository's check, archive the Change and prove the archived head; then propose, read both
forges' review runs, land and publish `dev` and `main`. To roll back the release, restore the
0.2.0-beta.11 declaration, without its Windows rows, in a new Change, then bind the retained runtime
with the current console's `hook install --runtime <0.2.0-beta.11 runtime>`. The Windows removal and
the label follow the owner's rulings and are not rolled back with the release; the old tags can
return only while the runners still carry them.
